identity.title: Hydronephrosis (bilateral or solitary kidney) on renal POCUS

technique.how: Curvilinear probe in the posterior axillary line (right ~ liver window, left higher and more posterior); obtain long and short axis of each kidney and fan through the entire organ. Hydronephrosis = anechoic dilatation of the renal pelvis and calyces; grade mild (pelvis only), moderate (calyces rounded), severe (cortical thinning). Always scan the bladder as well.
technique.prerequisites: Both kidneys imaged fully; know whether patient has a solitary or transplanted kidney; check bladder volume first because a full bladder causes mild bilateral pelvic dilatation.

interpretation.positive_finding: Unilateral hydronephrosis with flank pain suggests an obstructing stone (pooled LR+ 2.9; moderate-or-greater hydronephrosis specificity 0.94). Bilateral hydronephrosis, or hydronephrosis in a solitary/transplant kidney, with AKI indicates obstructive nephropathy needing decompression.
interpretation.negative_finding: No hydronephrosis makes obstructive AKI unlikely but does not exclude early obstruction, obstruction in a volume-depleted patient, or retroperitoneal fibrosis/encasement where the collecting system fails to dilate; LR- ~0.4 for stones.
interpretation.pitfalls: Full bladder, pregnancy, high-flow diuresis, extrarenal pelvis and parapelvic cysts mimic hydronephrosis; renal vessels can be mistaken for calyces (use color Doppler). Accuracy is strongly operator dependent (LR- 0.08 for fellowship-trained vs 0.37 overall).
interpretation.changes_what: Bilateral/solitary-kidney hydronephrosis with AKI: catheterize, urology for stent/nephrostomy. Unilateral with fever: infected obstruction until proven otherwise. None: seek other AKI causes.

estimates.target_condition: Nephrolithiasis (any degree of hydronephrosis on POCUS)
estimates.population: 1,773 adult ED patients with renal colic symptoms across 5 high-quality studies
estimates.reference_standard: CT evidence of stone or hydronephrosis, direct stone visualization, or surgical findings
estimates.quote: pooled results for sensitivity and specificity were 70.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 67.1%-73.2%) and 75.4% (95% CI = 72.5%-78.2%)

estimates.target_condition: Nephrolithiasis (moderate or greater hydronephrosis on POCUS)
estimates.population: Adult ED patients with renal colic in two of the meta-analysed studies
estimates.reference_standard: CT evidence of stone or hydronephrosis, direct stone visualization, or surgical findings
estimates.quote: moderate or greater hydronephrosis yielded a specificity of 94.4% (95% CI = 92.7%-95.8%)

estimates.population: 670 interpretable bedside scans in ED patients with suspected renal colic by 144 clinicians of all experience levels; 47.5% had hydronephrosis on CT
estimates.quote: sensitivity of 72.6% (95% confidence interval [CI] 65.4% to 78.9%), specificity of 73.3% (95% CI 66.1% to 79.4%)

estimates.target_condition: Hydronephrosis on CT (fellowship-trained emergency ultrasound attendings)
estimates.population: Subset of the same cohort scanned by attending physicians with emergency ultrasound fellowship training
estimates.quote: sensitivity of 92.7% (95% CI 83.8% to 96.9%), positive likelihood ratio of 4.97 (95% CI 2.90 to 8.51), and negative likelihood ratio of 0.08

sources.citation: Wong C, Teitge B, Ross M, Young P, Robertson HL, Lang E. The Accuracy and Prognostic Value of Point-of-care Ultrasound for Nephrolithiasis in the Emergency Department: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(6):684-698.

Herbst MK, Rosenberg G, Daniels B, et al. Effect of provider experience on clinician-performed ultrasonography for hydronephrosis in patients with suspected renal colic. Ann Emerg Med. 2014;64(3):269-276.
Riddell J, Case A, Wopat R, et al. Sensitivity of emergency bedside ultrasound to detect hydronephrosis in patients with computed tomography-proven stones. West J Emerg Med. 2014;15(1):96-100.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of hydronephrosis to exclude obstruction in hypovolemic or oliguric patients, retroperitoneal malignancy/fibrosis, or within the first hours of acute obstruction; do not diagnose obstruction from mild pelvic dilatation with a full bladder or in pregnancy without rescanning after voiding.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hydronephrosis with fever or sepsis is an infected obstructed system: cultures, IV antibiotics and emergent urology for decompression. Bilateral or solitary-kidney hydronephrosis with AKI or hyperkalemia: urgent decompression.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Herbst 2014: 144 clinicians; overall LR- 0.37 vs 0.08 for fellowship-trained attendings, and no accuracy gain with experience below fellowship level. Grading of mild vs moderate hydronephrosis is inconsistent between operators.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency clinician with basic renal POCUS training; pooled numbers reflect mixed experience (residents, PAs/NPs, attendings). Rule-out performance (LR- 0.08) applies only to fellowship-trained sonographers.

extraction_notes: All estimates are for ED renal-colic populations with CT reference; no study within the call budget quantified POCUS hydronephrosis specifically for obstructive AKI or bilateral/solitary-kidney obstruction, so the AKI use is inferred from the stone literature and should be flagged by the verifier. Wong 2018 LRs (2.85/0.39) are reported in the abstract without CIs. Riddell 2014 (retrospective, CT-proven stones only) sensitivity 78.4% cited as context, not entered because the population lacks a negative arm.
